summary: An informational memo written to calm worries that sending options in a TFTP request might make servers that do not understand options misbehave. It analyzes how such servers would react to the extended request and concludes the option scheme is safe to use. It specifies no standard.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo examines whether a TFTP client can send option information to a server that does not support option negotiation. The tested servers ignored the extra information and continued the transfer as before.

subtitle: A test of how unmodified TFTP servers handle option information.

tldr.problem: Implementers were concerned that TFTP servers without option negotiation might behave badly when a request included option information.
tldr.mechanism: The authors tested a modified client against five unmodified servers and examined BSD 4.3 TFTP server source code.
tldr.outcome: The tested servers ignored the options and proceeded as if no negotiation had been attempted, supporting backward compatibility with unmodified servers.

today: RFC 1785 is Informational and reports tests of TFTP option negotiation with unmodified servers. It concludes that those servers ignored the option information and proceeded normally.

sections.title: The Compatibility Concern
sections.content:
The TFTP option negotiation mechanism described in RFC 1782 is a backward-compatible extension that negotiates transfer options before file transfer. It uses a request, response, and acknowledgment sequence similar to TFTP's lock-step approach.

RFC 1785 addresses concerns that an option-bearing request might cause pathological behavior on servers that do not support option negotiation.
sections.plainLanguage: The option extension adds information to a TFTP request. The memo checks whether an older server can safely ignore that information.

sections.title: Testing Unmodified Servers
sections.content:
A client modified to send TFTP options was tested against five unmodified servers. In each test, the server ignored the option information and the transfer proceeded as if no option negotiation had been attempted.

The authors also examined BSD 4.3 TFTPD source code, which clearly ignored extra information in request packets. Based on these tests and source examination, the memo concludes that the mechanism is backward-compatible with unmodified TFTP servers.
sections.plainLanguage: All five tested servers ignored the options and continued normally. The BSD server code also ignored extra request information.

sections.title: Status of the Analysis
sections.content: RFC 1785 is an Informational analysis of TFTP option negotiation. It does not specify an Internet standard.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo reports compatibility tests; it does not define a new TFTP standard.

references.text: Malkin, G. and A. Harkin, "TFTP Option Extension", RFC 1782, March 1995.
